I need to identify the molecular formula of a compound in a sample. The only tool available is mass spectrometry with ESI (Electrospray Ionization) technique.

- Base peak at m/z 127.09971 (100% intensity)
- M+1 peak at m/z 128.10284 (8.12% intensity)
- M+2 peak at m/z 129.10511 (0.49% intensity)
- Additional smaller peaks

The base peak at m/z 127.09971 is likely the [M+H]+ ion (protonated molecular ion) in ESI positive mode, which is common for ESI-MS.

If m/z 127.09971 is [M+H]+, then the molecular weight would be approximately 126.09971.

Now I need to determine what molecular formula gives a mass of ~126.1:

Let me consider common organic compounds:
- C7H10O2: 7(12.011) + 10(1.008) + 2(15.999) = 84.077 + 10.08 + 31.998 = 126.155 (too high)

- C6H6O3: 6(12.011) + 6(1.008) + 3(15.999) = 72.066 + 6.048 + 47.997 = 126.111 (very close!)

Let me calculate C6H6O3 more precisely:
C6H6O3 = 6(12.0107) + 6(1.00783) + 3(15.9994) = 72.0642 + 6.04698 + 47.9982 = 126.10938

This is very close to 126.09971!

The M+1 peak intensity of 8.12% is consistent with the natural abundance of 13C (about 1.1% per carbon atom). For 6 carbons: 6 × 1.1% ≈ 6.6%, which is reasonably close to the observed 8.12%.

The molecular formula is C6H6O3.
